body:
## Problem

`TestCovMopConfigHandlersGetConfigPathError` fails on macOS (darwin). The helper `covMopXDGConfigAsFile`
points only `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` at a regular file, assuming that makes `xdg.ConfigFile` (and thus
`GetConfigPath`) fail. Unlike `xdg.CacheFile` (single candidate — the sibling cache test passes),
`xdg.ConfigFile` searches a fallback chain on darwin: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` →
`~/Library/Application Support` → `~/Library/Preferences` → `~/.config`. When the first candidate is a
file, xdg falls back to the next writable one and returns a valid path with no error, so the handlers'
error branch is never taken and both `configRootHandler`/`configInitHandler` return nil — the assertion
the test makes fail.

## Evidence

`go test ./...` on darwin (go 1.26.5):
```
--- FAIL: TestCovMopConfigHandlersGetConfigPathError (0.00s)
    coverage_mop_test.go:84: configRootHandler() expected error, got nil
    coverage_mop_test.go:87: configInitHandler() expected error, got nil
```
Reproduced in isolation (`go test -run '^TestCovMopConfigHandlersGetConfigPathError$'` → FAIL). An
experiment confirmed `GetConfigPath` returns `~/Library/Preferences/gh-action-readme/config.yaml`
(no error) when only `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is a file, but returns an error once `HOME` and
`XDG_CONFIG_DIRS` are also neutralized. Passes in CI because CI runs on Linux, where `xdg.ConfigFile`
has no `~/Library/*` fallbacks and the single `~/.config` candidate under a file-valued
`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` fails.

## Impact

Medium. `make test` / `go test ./...` is red on macOS — a primary supported dev platform (the repo's
own dev environment is darwin) — contradicting the project's "make test passes" invariant. The
coverage-mop test also fails to actually exercise the `GetConfigPath` error branch on darwin, so that
branch is untested locally despite the test existing for exactly that purpose.

## Fix

Make the helper neutralize every config candidate, not just `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (verified to force the
error on darwin):
```go
func covMopXDGConfigAsFile(t *testing.T) {
	t.Helper()
	dir := t.TempDir()
	seed := func(name string) string {
		p := filepath.Join(dir, name)
		if err := os.WriteFile(p, []byte("x"), 0o600); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("failed to seed %s: %v", name, err)
		}
		return p
	}
	t.Cleanup(xdg.Reload)
	t.Setenv("HOME", seed("home-is-a-file"))
	t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", seed("config-home-is-a-file"))
	t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_DIRS", "")
	xdg.Reload()
}
```
(Optionally apply the same HOME/XDG_CONFIG_DIRS hardening to `covMopXDGCacheAsFile` for consistency,
though the cache variant already passes.)

## Resolution
covMopXDGConfigAsFile now neutralizes HOME + XDG_CONFIG_HOME + XDG_CONFIG_DIRS so xdg.ConfigFile has no writable fallback on darwin; go test ./... green on macOS.
title: coverage_mop config-path error test fails on darwin — xdg.ConfigFile falls back past the bogus XDG_CONFIG_HOME

body:
## Problem

The go minor/patch packageRule sets `automerge: true` (`automergeType: pr`, `ignoreTests: false`) but no
`minimumReleaseAge` is set on that rule or at the top level. A dependency release that is compromised
(malicious minor/patch) is auto-merged as soon as CI passes. CI passing does not detect supply-chain
malice — it only proves the code compiles and tests run — so the malicious version can land on the
default branch before any human sees it. Semgrep flags this
(`renovate-missing-minimum-release-age`).

## Evidence

`.github/renovate.json`: the second `packageRules` entry (`matchDatasources: [go]`,
`matchUpdateTypes: [minor, patch]`) has `automerge: true` and no `minimumReleaseAge`. No
`minimumReleaseAge` appears anywhere in the local file. The config does `extends`
`github>ivuorinen/renovate-config`; if that shared preset already sets a `minimumReleaseAge`, this
finding is already mitigated — that must be verified in the preset repo (not visible here).

## Impact

Low. Window between a poisoned release being published and being auto-merged is minutes-to-hours
rather than zero, but for a maintainer-owned CLI the blast radius is limited and the extends-preset
may already cover it.

## Fix

Add a cooldown to the go minor/patch rule (or top level):
`"minimumReleaseAge": "3 days"`. If the shared preset already sets one, close this as invalid with a
note pointing at the preset line.

## Resolution
Added minimumReleaseAge: 3 days to the go minor/patch automerge rule in .github/renovate.json.
title: Renovate auto-merges go minor/patch with no minimumReleaseAge cooldown

## Problem

`gen -f html` produces an HTML file whose `<title>` contains the literal
template placeholder `{{.Name}}` instead of the action name. The HTML wrapper
markup is not passed through the template engine, so its placeholders leak into
the output verbatim.

## Evidence

Built from current `chore/updates` and ran:
`gar gen testdata/example-action/ -f html -o /tmp/gv/html`
Head of the produced `Example Action.html`:
```
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>{{.Name}} GitHub Action Documentation</title>
```
`{{.Name}}` should have rendered to `Example Action`.

## Impact

Every HTML document generated by the tool ships a broken, unrendered title.
`-f html` is an advertised output format; its primary output is malformed.

## Fix

Render the HTML wrapper (the `<!DOCTYPE html>…</title>…` shell in the HTML
template/`HTMLWriter` path) through the same `html/template` execution that
receives `TemplateData`, so `{{.Name}}` and any other placeholders in the
wrapper are evaluated. Add a generation test asserting the output title equals
the action name, not the literal `{{.Name}}`.

## Resolution
RenderReadme now executes header/footer through the template engine via renderPartial (internal/template.go); HTML <title> renders the action name. Verified end-to-end + regression test TestRenderReadme_HTMLHeaderPlaceholders.

## Problem

`validateHandler(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string)` discards `args` and always
validates the current working directory via `helpers.GetCurrentDir()`. A path
passed to `validate <path>` has no effect, and a nonexistent path does not
error.

"Validation Summary for 5 files" instead of erroring on the bad path.

Users pointing `validate` at a specific action/dir silently validate the wrong
tree. CI that runs `validate path/to/action` gets a false pass/fail based on CWD
contents, not the intended target.

Consume `args`: when a path is provided, validate that path (erroring if it does
not exist); fall back to CWD only when no arg is given. Add a test that
`validate <nonexistent>` returns an error and `validate <dir>` scopes to that dir.

## Problem

`deps pin` is documented as "Convert floating versions (like @v4) to pinned
commit SHAs with version comments." Its command registration reuses
`depsUpgradeHandler` (`cmd_deps.go:74` — "Uses same handler with different
flags"). The upgrade handler pins floating deps to the SHA of the *latest*
release, so `pin` silently upgrades versions rather than pinning the currently
referenced version.

## Evidence

`cmd_deps.go:74` `Run: wrapHandlerWithErrorHandling(depsUpgradeHandler)` for
`pinCmd`. Documented behavior (pin the existing floating ref to its SHA) differs
from upgrade behavior (resolve to newest, then pin). e.g. `actions/checkout@v4`
becomes `actions/checkout@<sha> # v6.0.3` rather than the SHA for v4.

## Impact

`pin` changes dependency *versions*, not just their reference form. A user who
wants to lock current versions to SHAs unknowingly bumps them to the latest
major — the opposite of a conservative pin.

## Fix

Give `pin` its own handler (or a mode flag on the shared handler) that resolves
each floating ref to the SHA of the *currently referenced* tag without version
bumping. Add a test asserting `pin` on `@v4` yields the SHA of v4, not the latest.

## Resolution
Added Analyzer.GeneratePinInPlace + collectPinUpdates; deps pin now pins each floating ref to the SHA of its CURRENT tag (no upgrade) instead of reusing the upgrade collection. Skips already-pinned/local/shell/branch refs. Test TestGeneratePinInPlace.
title: deps pin reuses the upgrade handler, so it upgrades instead of pinning as-is

The global `-q/--quiet` flag ("quiet output (overrides verbose)") suppresses the
entire output of query commands whose sole purpose is to print a value.
`cache path` and `cache stats` emit their result through `output.Printf`, which

`AppConfig` loads/merges `Permissions`, `RunsOn`, `ShowSecurityInfo`, and
`Variables`, and the wizard prompts for them, but no generator or template ever
reads them. They are accepted (and documented) config keys with no effect on

## Problem

`.claude/rules/context-mode-required.md` mandates that context-producing commands
(`go test`, builds, grep/find/cat, git log/diff, large output) be routed through
the context-mode tool, and **explicitly forbids** bypassing it with the `# ctx-ok`
escape. CLAUDE.md repeats this. But no hook enforces it. The mandate is honored
only by agent goodwill.

Harness: Claude Code (`.claude/` present; no AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md/copilot marker).
A qualifying context-saving tool IS installed (context-mode `ctx_execute` /
`ctx_batch_execute` / `ctx_execute_file`), so the routing-finding precondition holds.

## Evidence

Hook inventory (`.claude/settings.json`):
- PreToolUse Bash → `pre-bash-dangerous-guard.sh` — guards ONLY destruction
  (`--no-verify`, force-push, `rm -rf /|~`); it does no context routing.
- PreToolUse Edit|Write → sensitive-file + readme guards. PostToolUse Edit|Write →
  go-lint + yaml-format. None touch Bash output routing.

The context-mode plugin's own PreToolUse:Bash hook only injects `additionalContext`
(an advisory "tip"); it does not emit a `permissionDecision`, so every gather
command runs regardless. Observed all session: `grep`/`find`/`ls`/`git log` via raw
Bash executed with only a tip attached, never denied.

Result: a `grep -rn`, `go test ./...`, `git log`, or `cat big.log` run in raw Bash
dumps full output into the conversation with nothing blocking it — the exact
context-window bloat the rule exists to prevent. `# ctx-ok` can be appended to
anything with no check, despite the rule forbidding it.

## Impact

The project's central context-discipline mandate is unenforceable in practice:
any agent (or subagent) that forgets — or deliberately bypasses via `# ctx-ok` —
silently violates it, bloating context and degrading the rest of the session.
This is the failure class the rule was written to stop, left wholly unguarded.

## Fix

Add a PreToolUse(Bash) routing hook `.claude/hooks/pre-bash-context-mode-guard.sh`
wired in `.claude/settings.json` under the existing `"matcher": "Bash"` block. It
emits `permissionDecision: deny` (documented block) for context-producing/gather
verbs not on the must-run-direct allowlist, names the `ctx_*` tool to use instead,
does NOT honor `# ctx-ok` for those verbs, and fails closed on malformed input.

Proven behavior (fired on stdin payloads before wiring):
- DENY: `grep -rn`, `go test ./...`, `git log`, `cat`, `find`, `make test-coverage-check`,
  `ps aux | wc -l`, and `grep ... # ctx-ok` (bypass correctly still denied).
- ALLOW: `git status`, `git commit -m "...grep..."` (allowlist short-circuit — not
  fooled by 'grep' in the message), `go build`, `mkdir`, `pwd`.
- Fail-closed DENY on unparseable input; empty command allowed.

Script staged at scratchpad `pre-bash-context-mode-guard.sh` pending approval to
wire (a Bash-deny hook changes day-to-day tool behavior, so it needs explicit
per-change consent per the agent-hooks fix strategy).

## Resolution
Added .claude/hooks/pre-bash-context-mode-guard.sh (PreToolUse Bash, permissionDecision:deny, fail-closed, does not honor '# ctx-ok') and wired it in settings.json alongside pre-bash-dangerous-guard.sh. Proven via the wired settings path: grep/go test/git log/cat/find/make test-*/…|wc and the # ctx-ok bypass all DENY; git status/commit/go build/mkdir/pwd ALLOW; malformed input fails closed. Not committed.
title: context-mode routing mandate has no enforcing hook — only an advisory nudge

## Problem

arch-profile.md Inferred Structural Rule 10 mandates reading the GitHub token via internal.GetGitHubToken(config) and never touching config.GitHubToken directly (except loader/merge/redaction sites). The project cares enough to ship a dedicated `token-security-reviewer` subagent for it — yet no always-on .claude/rules file captures it, so the main agent gets the guidance only when that subagent is explicitly invoked.

## Evidence

docs/audit/arch-profile.md "Inferred Structural Rules" #10. Subagent `token-security-reviewer` exists ("verifies GetGitHubToken() is used everywhere instead of direct config.GitHubToken field access"). Neither CLAUDE.md (207 lines) nor any .claude/rules/ file states it.

## Impact

Regression risk on a security-relevant accessor; enforcement depends on remembering to run a subagent rather than standing context injection (which _conventions notes is more reliable for security mandates).

## Fix

Create .claude/rules/github-token-accessor.md, path-scoped to "**/*.go": "Always read the GitHub token via `internal.GetGitHubToken(config)`. Never read `config.GitHubToken` directly, except in the config loader/merge/redaction sites that legitimately set or scrub the field."

## Resolution
Created .claude/rules/github-token-accessor.md (path-scoped **/*.go); anatomy checker passes.
title: New rule candidate: GetGitHubToken() is the canonical token accessor (arch rule 10, has a subagent, no always-on rule)

## Problem

arch-profile.md Inferred Structural Rule 9 mandates that only _test.go files import testutil; production code must not. This has been violated repeatedly (multiple resolved arch findings) and has a dedicated audit surface, but no .claude/rules file enforces it always-on.

## Evidence

docs/audit/arch-profile.md "Inferred Structural Rules" #9 ("Production code must not import testutil ... Confirmed: zero production files import it"). resolved.jsonl arch findings: "Three test-helper files import `testutil` without `_test.go`", "internal/testoutput.go ships test doubles in production-code", "internal/dependencies/updater_test_helper.go imports testutil".

## Impact

The boundary regresses easily (a helper file dropped without the _test.go suffix leaks test-only code into the shipped binary) and is only caught by a full arch audit.

## Fix

Create .claude/rules/no-testutil-in-production.md: "Never import `testutil` from a non-test file. Only `_test.go` files may import `testutil`. Test helpers shared across tests must live in `*_test.go` files (or a test-tagged file), never in production `.go` files."

## Resolution
Created .claude/rules/no-testutil-in-production.md; anatomy checker passes.
